slides.title: The pathway outlives the cable by decades.
slides.body: Choose the wrong conduit and every future cable pays for it.

slides.title: Rigid PVC: straight and stiff
slides.body: Ten or twenty foot sticks, solvent cemented. Made for open trenches and concrete-encased duct banks. Too stiff to drill.

slides.title: HDPE: flexible, on reels
slides.body: Long continuous lengths that bend. The pipe behind directional drills, ploughs and micro-trenchers. Lower SDR, thicker wall.

slides.title: Innerduct splits big pipes
slides.body: Three 1.25 inch innerducts in a 4 inch duct gives three pathways. New cables never rub against old ones.

slides.title: India's standard duct
slides.body: Permanently lubricated HDPE in 40/33 mm and 50/42 mm. Most cable is blown into it, not pulled.

PVC suits straight trenches and encased duct banks, HDPE goes behind the drill and the plough, and innerduct turns one big pipe into several pathways. Swipe for when to use each.
